nodes.norm_label: note: no memberid in the input schema. a lint rule (no-member-id-in-request-...

nodes.label: NOTE: $onUpdate only fires through Drizzle; migration 0001 also installs a
nodes.norm_label: note: $onupdate only fires through drizzle; migration 0001 also installs a

nodes.label: No Cross-Module JOINs
nodes.rationale: No cross-module infrastructure/, schema.ts or JOINs across Postgres schemas.

nodes.label: Better Auth Access Control
nodes.rationale: Operator JWTs come from Better Auth; Better Auth access control is derived from the same permission-to-role map via toAccessControlRoles() so roles are not declared twice.

nodes.label: auth pgSchema owned by Identity
nodes.rationale: Better Auth auth.* is generated then moved into pgSchema("auth") and owned by identity; the internal id is auth.user.id (ours), never a provider id.

nodes.label: Dev Sender Refused In Production
nodes.rationale: console sender never used when NODE_ENV=production.

nodes.label: Do Not Touch Without An ADR
nodes.norm_label: do not touch without an adr

nodes.label: Done Means bun run validate Green
nodes.norm_label: done means bun run validate green

nodes.label: Three Enforcement Tools
nodes.rationale: exports maps for compiler visibility; dependency-cruiser for layers/cross-module/cycles; eslint-plugin-boundaries plus custom rules for intra-module layering, memberId, inline colors, testID, floating promises, env casts, forEach-async.

nodes.label: Unencoded Rules Do Not Exist
nodes.rationale: A rule that is not encoded here does not exist; adding a rule means adding a check plus a test that a violation fails.

nodes.label: Targeting XOR Constraint
nodes.rationale: targeting XOR target_member_id CHECK.

nodes.label: drizzle-orm 1.x Relational Queries v2
nodes.rationale: Stay on 1.x to avoid a relations v1 to v2 migration after nine modules; native through for M:N.

nodes.label: Canonical Idempotent Seed Fixture
nodes.rationale: Idempotent fixture that refuses production, from the Drizzle guide lesson of TRUNCATE without a guard.

nodes.label: Intra-schema defineRelations
nodes.rationale: defineRelations composed from per-module parts, intra-schema only, because a cross-schema relation is a forbidden cross-module JOIN.

nodes.label: Explicit Column Names
nodes.rationale: No casing magic because the Drizzle casing API changed between 0.x and 1.0; explicit names do not change.

nodes.label: Database UUID v4 Identifiers
nodes.rationale: uuid v4 from Postgres on PG 16 on the VPS; uuid v7 when moving to PG 18; temporal order comes from indexed created_at rather than the id.

nodes.label: Opaque IDs Across Modules
nodes.rationale: FKs with onDelete only inside a module. Across modules: opaque ids plus events plus idempotent handlers plus the zero-rows deletion test.

nodes.label: RQB v2 Relations Parts per Module
nodes.norm_label: rqb v2 relations parts per module
nodes.rationale: A relations part may reference only its own schema's tables (enforced by test/relations.test.ts). Cross-module reads are facade calls or events, never relations.

nodes.label: One File per Postgres Schema
nodes.rationale: Each Postgres schema is one owning module: platform, auth, members, notifications, proposals, engagement, crm, personalization. Explicit column names; no casing magic. After stage 0 day 4 files move next to modules; this package keeps the re-export index.

nodes.label: Synthetic UUID Primary Keys
nodes.rationale: PK is a synthetic uuid; business logic is never a PK; the auth provider's id is never a key anywhere.

nodes.label: At-Least-Once Delivery
nodes.rationale: Does not guarantee global ordering or exactly-once for external side effects; handlers must be idempotent. No delivery while a consumer is paused. Six retries with exponential backoff then DLQ (DLQ after 7 attempts in tests).

nodes.label: Platform Alerts
nodes.rationale: Alert when oldest pending delivery is older than 5 minutes, on any DLQ row, or when a job has no successful run in 36 hours.

nodes.label: Platform Facade API
nodes.rationale: src/api/index.ts exposes events.{defineEvent, registerConsumer, publish, tombstoneMember}, flags, jobs, poller (host only), logger, metrics, and health().

nodes.label: Platform-Owned Jobs
nodes.rationale: Jobs owned: partitions, retention, queue-health. Invariants include job singleton/record/failure.

nodes.label: GET /metrics
nodes.rationale: Exposes queue depth, oldest pending age, DLQ, and job durations; jobs.lastRuns() answers whether a job ran.

nodes.label: platform.poller
nodes.rationale: poller.start() is one line; SKIP LOCKED makes several instances safe. poller.replay(id) replays a dead delivery.

nodes.label: Delete Equals Zero Rows
nodes.rationale: deleteAccount leaves zero rows plus a journal tombstone.

nodes.label: Activity Exactly Once By external_id
nodes.rationale: CRM down → retry; activity created exactly once after recovery via external_id.

nodes.label: D5 Enforcement Tooling
nodes.rationale: cruiser, eslint boundaries, validate, CI, CODEOWNERS, PR template; a forbidden import fails CI.

nodes.label: @bbc/api
nodes.rationale: The host. buildApp() does six things and nothing else.

nodes.label: buildApp()
nodes.rationale: Does six things and nothing else: env → db + platform → modules in layer order (ports satisfied from earlier facades, killed modules skipped) → middleware in fixed order → routes (Better Auth, module routes, jobs) → poller.

nodes.label: drainAll()
nodes.rationale: Drives the poller so nobody waits on timers.

nodes.label: middleware
nodes.rationale: Installed in fixed order during buildApp().

nodes.label: modules
nodes.rationale: Loaded in layer order with ports satisfied from earlier facades; killed modules skipped. Adding a module is one line in src/modules.ts. If its consumers have no handler at boot, or it asks for a port from a higher layer, boot fails — on purpose.

nodes.label: routes
nodes.rationale: Host routes are Better Auth, module routes, and jobs.

nodes.label: shutdown()
nodes.rationale: Stops the poller after the in-flight delivery and closes the pool; SIGTERM calls it.

nodes.label: No Expo Push Service
nodes.rationale: Out of scope: Expo Push Service; notifications decide who gets what.

nodes.label: Layer-order module boot
nodes.rationale: Modules load in layer order; ports are satisfied from earlier facades; killed modules are skipped. If consumers have no handler at boot, or a module asks for a port from a higher layer, boot fails on purpose.

nodes.label: Thin Host
nodes.rationale: buildApp() does six things and nothing else: env → db + platform → modules in layer order → middleware in fixed order → routes → poller.

nodes.label: linked IFF crm_client_id Present
nodes.rationale: CHECK: linked ⇔ crm_client_id present.

nodes.label: Transactional Bypasses Consent
nodes.rationale: Transactional notifications bypass consent and quiet hours.

nodes.label: No Model On Request Path
nodes.rationale: Out of scope: online inference; v2 = batch scores table.

nodes.label: actorMemberId Async Principal
nodes.rationale: Async handlers run as system with actorMemberId taken from the event; repositories stay scoped identically to the request path so ownership checks do not weaken off the HTTP path.

nodes.label: no-member-id-in-request-schemas Lint
nodes.rationale: Any Zod request schema in packages/shared that contains memberId fails CI so clients cannot supply the identity used for ownership scoping.

nodes.label: Authorization Principals
nodes.rationale: Three principal kinds: member via session cookie, operator via Better Auth JWT with role=operator, and system via X-Internal-Secret on /v1/internal/* or JWT role=system for handlers and cron.

nodes.label: Actor Comes From Principal
nodes.rationale: No memberId/userId in any request schema. Ownership is in the SQL WHERE; someone else's resource is a 404.

nodes.label: Consumer ctx.principal
nodes.rationale: ctx.principal is system plus actorMemberId from the event so repositories stay scoped on the async path.

nodes.label: Ownership in SQL WHERE
nodes.rationale: Second enforcement layer: scoped repositories put ownership in the SQL WHERE using member id from the principal only. Missing or foreign resource returns 404 rather than 403, so IDOR does not leak existence.

nodes.label: memberId In Body Ignored
nodes.rationale: memberId in body ignored; actor is the principal.

nodes.label: Modules Scaffolded With Failing Contract Test
nodes.norm_label: modules scaffolded with failing contract test
nodes.rationale: A new module cannot be green by accident; it.todo keeps validate red.

nodes.label: 0001_extras.sql
nodes.rationale: Extras after drizzle-kit DDL: updated_at trigger, monthly partitioning of platform.domain_events, and platform.cross_schema_fks view. scripts/migrate.ts applies drizzle output plus extras under an advisory lock and exits 1 on failure.

nodes.label: pg_try_advisory_xact_lock
nodes.rationale: Combined with SKIP LOCKED so only one poller or dispatcher is active and work is not duplicated; migrations also run under an advisory lock.

nodes.label: Expand/Contract Migrations
nodes.rationale: drizzle-kit generate, review, then migrate under advisory lock with exit(1) on failure; extras SQL after DDL because triggers and partitioning are not expressible in Drizzle.

nodes.label: FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
nodes.rationale: Queue workers use FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED so multiple pollers do not process the same row.

nodes.label: ADR-ARCH-001 Schema per Module
nodes.rationale: One Postgres schema per module and no cross-module foreign keys; a cross-schema relation would be a cross-module JOIN under another name, caught by an automated test.

nodes.label: ATS Hero Schema Lessons
nodes.rationale: Applied lessons: real XOR, internal id, enum in the database, atomic counter, expiry, and cascade.

nodes.label: bumpCounter
nodes.rationale: Atomic upsert with optional cap, tested with 25 concurrent increments.

nodes.label: db:verify Fitness Functions
nodes.rationale: Eight live-database checks so guide rules become CI rather than review.

nodes.label: Live DB Fitness Functions
nodes.rationale: scripts/verify.ts on the live DB after migrate: schemas exist, no cross-schema FK, every *_id indexed, no naive timestamps, created_at everywhere, trigger on every updated_at, status columns are enums, journal is partitioned.

nodes.label: Invariants in the Database
nodes.rationale: pgEnum for states, CHECK for ranges and XOR consistency, UNIQUE scoped to the parent for idempotency, NOT NULL explicit. Proven by schema tests with zero application code, including XOR, idempotency key, and 25 concurrent counter increments.

nodes.label: createDb
nodes.rationale: Single factory createDb(url, opts) sets pool sizing, statement_timeout 15s, withTx, and the Executor type.

nodes.label: withTx
nodes.rationale: Use cases open the transaction; repositories accept a db or a transaction via Executor.

nodes.label: platform.events.publish
nodes.rationale: Publishing is only possible with a transaction in hand; the sample writes an offer then publishes offer.published inside withTx.

nodes.label: Connection Pool Sizing
nodes.rationale: App pool 10, scripts 1, statement_timeout 15s because Bun is one process and nothing on the request path should run longer than 15 seconds.

nodes.label: Transactional Outbox
nodes.rationale: Events are written in the same transaction as the use-case state change so a rollback cannot leave an event without the corresponding row.

nodes.label: withTx Use-Case Transactions
nodes.rationale: The use case opens withTx and repositories receive an Executor so domain events can be written in the same transaction as the state change (outbox).

nodes.label: events.publish inside Transaction
nodes.rationale: Repositories take an Executor; use cases open the transaction; events.publish(tx, …) rides inside it. Raw sql only in infrastructure for SKIP LOCKED, advisory locks, and partition DDL.

nodes.label: resource:action Permissions
nodes.rationale: Permissions are resource:action strings declared once here and mapped to roles, then projected into Better Auth.

nodes.label: platform.flags
nodes.rationale: Flags fail-safe; used to pause a consumer without a deploy.

nodes.label: authorize(permission) Route Layer
nodes.rationale: First enforcement layer: authorize(permission) on every route, deny by default, inventoried via routeRegistry plus an inventory test. Wrong role returns 403; wrong secret returns 401.

nodes.label: Module Killswitch
nodes.rationale: Per-module killswitch is treated as module-level authorization: the API returns 503 and the BFF falls back, without a deploy.

nodes.label: Killswitch Makes rank Refuse
nodes.rationale: killswitch → rank refuses, BFF falls back.

nodes.label: Modules Talk Two Ways Only
nodes.rationale: Direct calls through another module api/index.ts for questions; events through platform.events.publish(tx) for facts.

nodes.label: Segment Evaluation In SQL
nodes.rationale: Segment evaluation in SQL; broadcast throttled through notifications never bypassing consent.

nodes.label: At-Least-Once Plus Idempotent
nodes.rationale: Handlers may run twice; use unique keys and upserts. Check state at action time, not when queued.

nodes.label: platform.* Schema
nodes.rationale: Owns domain_events (partitioned monthly), event_deliveries, event_dlq, external_inbox, flags, job_runs, and rate_limits. Publishes nothing and consumes nothing; it is the mechanism other modules publish and consume through.

nodes.label: events.registerConsumer
nodes.rationale: ctx.tx also marks the delivery done so handler writes and processed commit together.

nodes.label: registerModules
nodes.rationale: Each module calls registerConsumer and jobs.register during boot after events are defined and platform jobs are registered.

nodes.label: Per-aggregate_id Ordering
nodes.rationale: Order is guaranteed per aggregate_id, never globally.

nodes.label: Atomic Event plus Deliveries
nodes.rationale: Event and deliveries are written in the caller's transaction, atomic with the state change. Handler writes and delivery status commit together. Invariant: rollback means no event.

nodes.label: Report DESIGN.md Conflicts
nodes.rationale: Report any conflict between DESIGN.md and code instead of resolving it silently.

nodes.label: postgres-test
nodes.rationale: Throwaway in-RAM test database, fast. Never used for anything but bun test. fsync, synchronous_commit, and full_page_writes are off; data lives on tmpfs.

nodes.label: Demo 2
nodes.rationale: The smoke test is Demo 2 in code.

nodes.label: testAuth
nodes.rationale: Creates real members and returns real session cookies and an operator JWT.

nodes.label: tmpfs
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL data directory is mounted on tmpfs so the test database stays in RAM and is discarded with the container.

nodes.label: ADR-IMPL-006 Authorization Enforcement
nodes.rationale: Named ADR for how BBC Club authorization is enforced: principals, resource:action permissions, two enforcement layers, async system actors, and a per-module killswitch.

nodes.label: Identity Consumes Nothing
nodes.rationale: core/identity publishes member.registered and member.deleted and consumes no domain events.

nodes.label: Delete Equals Zero Rows Plus Tombstone
nodes.norm_label: delete equals zero rows plus tombstone
nodes.rationale: Account deletion must leave zero identity rows and emit a tombstone, covered by delete.test.

nodes.label: Not in v1 2FA Social Admin Impersonation
nodes.norm_label: not in v1 2fa social admin impersonation
nodes.rationale: v1 identity excludes 2FA (TOTP/OTP), social login, admin dashboard, impersonation, and avatars.

nodes.label: Post-hook Outside Better Auth Transaction
nodes.rationale: member.registered is published in a post-hook outside Better Auth's transaction, so members.reconcileMissingProfiles runs nightly to backfill missing profiles.
